To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dissemination, implementation, translation, and sustainability are complex processes that require a range of strategies and approaches that are context specific.

(i) there is a need to develop a more comprehensive understanding of the factors that facilitate or impede the uptake of research evidence into policy and clinical practice in different settings, cultures, and contexts; (ii) there are many different theories that can be used to guide the development and testing of interventions to promote the translation of research evidence into clinical practice; (iii) the use of theory is critical in developing and testing interventions to promote the uptake of research into practice and policy; (iv)

the use of a range of theories and research methodologies can be used to improve the translation of behavioral medicine research findings into policy and practice in both developed and resource-poor countries.

the science of dissemination and implementation of evidence-based behavioral medicine in diverse populations in different settings, and the translation of this research into public health practice.
how to best translate and disseminate research into practice and policy in order to improve health, wellbeing, and quality of life for all.
the science of dissemination and implementation in behavioral medicine and the translation of evidence-based behavioral medicine interventions into policy, practice, and public health.
